before.known: When did you start?
before.target: ¿Cuándo empezaste a?

evidence: The question ends with a stranded infinitival preposition a. The export gives S0079L02B03 with the same known and ¿Cuándo empezaste?; the sibling USE rows supply a following infinitive when a is present.

before.known: I was thinking much about your friend
before.target: Estaba pensando mucho sobre tu amigo

after.known: I was thinking a lot about your friend

evidence: Affirmative I was thinking much about your friend is unnatural. S0083L03U04 already models thinking a lot about your friend with the same mucho construction.

before.known: he said something
before.target: Él dijo algo

evidence: The exported group he said something also contains S0342L01B01 → dijo algo. Removing the optional subject pronoun standardises the structural variant and retains dijo.

before.known: My friend
before.target: Mi amigo

evidence: The exported my friend group maps this prompt to mi amigo and S0284L02B02 to Mi amiga. The prompt does not distinguish gender; a repair must resolve the course-wide sense split while preserving this LEGO.

before.known: still
before.target: todavía

evidence: The exported still group maps to todavía here and aún at seed 593. Both mean still; this bare prompt has two targets. Retargeting to aún would remove the required todavía.

before.known: I'm very happy with everything I have done already
before.target: Estoy muy contento con lo que he hecho ya

after.known: I'm very happy with what I have done already

evidence: Everything is not expressed by lo que he hecho; compare sibling U08 todo lo que for everything. The replacement matches the existing target.

before.known: I have done a lot today but I want to learn more
before.target: He hecho mucho hoy pero quiero aprender más todavía

after.target: He hecho mucho hoy pero quiero aprender más

evidence: Target adds todavía, still, to the wish to learn more. The known has no still or yet; removing it preserves he hecho and uses only existing words.

before.known: It would be good if I can speak Spanish faster
before.target: Sería bueno si puedo hablar español más rápido

after.known: It would be good to be able to speak Spanish faster
after.target: Sería bueno poder hablar español más rápido

evidence: Sería bueno si puedo combines would with a present indicative condition. S0090L04B04/U03 supplies the clean sería bueno poder construction, avoiding an untaught imperfect subjunctive.

before.known: That's great that you want to help me learn Spanish with you
before.target: Eso es genial que quieres ayudarme a aprender español contigo

after.known: You want to help me learn Spanish with you and that's great
after.target: Quieres ayudarme a aprender español contigo y eso es genial

evidence: Eso es genial que quieres is malformed as an evaluation of a subordinate proposition: it requires es genial que plus subjunctive. Reordering the same content avoids introducing quieras ahead of seed 97.

before.known: It would be great if I could speak Spanish as fast as possible
before.target: Sería genial si puedo hablar español lo más rápido posible

after.known: It would be great to be able to speak Spanish as fast as possible
after.target: Sería genial poder hablar español lo más rápido posible

evidence: English if I could is rendered si puedo, if I can. The sibling B06 models sería genial poder, which expresses the intended possibility without new inflections.

before.known: I'm not speaking quickly enough but I'm trying to improve
before.target: No estoy hablando lo suficientemente rápido pero estoy intentando aprender

after.known: I'm not speaking quickly enough but I'm trying to learn

evidence: The target ends intentando aprender, trying to learn, rather than trying to improve. The replacement keeps the target and the required lo suficientemente rápido.

before.known: This
before.target: Esto

evidence: The exported this group maps this bare prompt to Esto here and Este at S0126L01B01. The English supplies no grammatical context to select the demonstrative form; no course-wide resolution is available within this window.

before.known: For a while
before.target: Por un rato

evidence: The exported for a while group maps to Por un rato here and Un rato at seed 219. These are structural variants of the same duration; removing por would not resolve the bare un rato/for a while LEGO collision elsewhere.

before.known: I don't think it will work
before.target: No pienso que va a funcionar

after.known: I think it will not work
after.target: Pienso que no va a funcionar

evidence: No pienso que normally selects subjunctive vaya, rather than va, in this negative belief statement. Moving the negation into the subordinate clause retains the exact va a funcionar LEGO without introducing a new form.

before.known: I don't think it will work
before.target: No pienso que va a funcionar

after.known: I think it will not work
after.target: Pienso que no va a funcionar

evidence: No pienso que normally selects subjunctive vaya, rather than va, in this negative belief statement. Moving the negation into the subordinate clause retains the exact va a funcionar LEGO without introducing a new form.

before.known: I don't think this will work
before.target: No pienso que esto va a funcionar

after.known: I think this will not work
after.target: Pienso que esto no va a funcionar

evidence: Negative no pienso que esto va requires subjunctive in this ordinary reading. Affirmative pienso que with subordinate negation preserves va a funcionar and the intended negative prediction.

before.known: I don't understand yet
before.target: Todavía no entiendo

evidence: The same English prompt occurs in sibling B04 with No entiendo todavía. Standardise this USE to that order; both versions retain todavía.

before.known: I don't know yet how to say enough words
before.target: No sé cómo decir suficientes palabras diferentes todavía

after.target: No sé cómo decir suficientes palabras todavía

evidence: The target adds diferentes, different, to enough words. The known does not request different words. Removing that adjective preserves todavía and introduces no vocabulary.

before.known: I still want to keep doing this for a while
before.target: Todavía me gustaría seguir haciendo esto por un rato

after.known: I'd still like to keep doing this for a while

evidence: Me gustaría expresses would like, whereas the known says want. S0092L03 supplies the would like to continue for a while pattern.

before.known: I want to do what you want whenever you want
before.target: Quiero hacer algo cuando quieras

after.known: I want to do something whenever you want

evidence: Quiero hacer algo means I want to do something. It does not express the embedded what you want in the current known.

before.known: I think I should try to speak more quickly
before.target: Pienso que debería intentar hablar lo más rápido posible

after.known: I think I should try to speak as fast as possible

evidence: Lo más rápido posible is as fast as possible, not merely more quickly. That exact construction appears in S0090L05U12.

before.known: I think I need to consider what to say
before.target: Pienso que necesito considerar lo que quiero decir

after.known: I think I need to consider what I want to say

evidence: The target explicitly includes quiero, I want. What to say omits that intention; sibling U04 already supplies the matching known phrase.

before.known: I think it is not working because I am not trying well enough
before.target: Pienso que no está funcionando porque no estoy intentando lo suficientemente bien

evidence: Trying well enough is not the ordinary expression for insufficient effort; trying hard enough would be. Spanish intentando lo suficientemente bien likewise leaves intentar without an action and substitutes manner for effort. No clean replacement proposed with verified taught vocabulary.

before.known: No need to worry
before.target: No hay por qué preocuparte

evidence: Impersonal no hay por qué requires preocuparse; personal preocuparte naturally requires no tienes por qué. Neither correction can retain this exact LEGO while relying on verified earlier vocabulary.

before.known: There is no need to worry about that right now
before.target: No hay por qué preocuparte por eso ahora

evidence: No hay por qué preocuparte mixes an impersonal construction with a second-person reflexive. A normal repair is no tienes por qué preocuparte or no hay por qué preocuparse; no replacement proposed under the containment and vocabulary restrictions.

before.known: Do not worry about how fast you are learning
before.target: No deberías preocuparte por lo rápido que estás aprendiendo

after.known: You should not worry about how fast you are learning

evidence: The target says no deberías, you should not, rather than the direct instruction do not worry. The sibling U01 establishes the matching should not worry wording.

before.known: There is no need to worry at all
before.target: No hay por qué preocuparte de nada

evidence: No hay por qué preocuparte has the same impersonal/personal mismatch as B04 and U05. De nada also means about anything, while the English uses at all. No constrained replacement proposed.

before.known: You do not need to worry because I can help you
before.target: No hay por qué preocuparte porque puedo ayudarte

evidence: No hay por qué preocuparte mixes impersonal hay with personal te. The target needs a different construction; no replacement proposed without verified availability of tienes.

before.known: The important thing is not to worry about doing it slowly
before.target: Lo importante es no preocuparte por hacer eso despacio

after.known: The important thing is not to worry about doing that slowly

evidence: The target uses hacer eso, doing that; the known uses doing it. The replacement preserves the existing target and por hacer.

before.known: Do not worry about doing it differently from everyone else
before.target: No deberías preocuparte por hacer eso diferente de todos los demás

after.known: You should not worry about doing that differently from everyone else

evidence: No deberías is you should not, not the imperative do not; hacer eso is doing that. The replacement explicitly matches both existing target elements.

before.known: She told me she was not worried about doing that
before.target: Ella me dijo que no debería preocuparte por hacer eso

problem: Meaning mismatch and Spanish person agreement
evidence: The known reports that she was not worried. The target instead says she told me that I should not worry, with debería and second-person preocuparte also mismatched. No clean replacement proposed under the constraints.

before.known: The most important thing is not to worry about doing everything perfectly
before.target: Lo más importante es no preocuparte por hacer todo bien

after.known: The most important thing is not to worry about doing everything well

evidence: Hacer todo bien means doing everything well, not perfectly. The replacement uses the established well/bien gloss without changing the target.

before.known: He asked me to try something similar with his dog
before.target: Él quiere intentar algo parecido con su perro

after.known: He wants to try something similar with his dog

evidence: Él quiere intentar says he wants to try. It does not say he asked me to try: neither asked nor me is present. The replacement keeps parecido and the entire target.
